s1.syndrome_frame: Gradual-onset unilateral facial weakness with a mass in the ear canal
salient_findings: Nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal
Mild sensorineural hearing loss at 4000 Hz
key_facts: 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness
Initially treated with oral steroids
No hearing loss, tinnitus, imbalance, or other cranial nerve deficits
Nonpulsatile mass in the inferior ear canal
Mild sensorineural hearing loss at 4000 Hz
Irregular lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen on MRI
Expansion of the fallopian canal and erosion of the posterior external auditory canal on CT
Specimen consisted of cartilage on gross examination
Pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei on microscopic examination

shortlist.label: Facial nerve schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Gradual-onset unilateral facial weakness with a mass in the ear canal and imaging findings of a lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen

shortlist.label: Chondrosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Specimen consisted of cartilage on gross examination and microscopic examination showed pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei in a myxochondroid matrix

shortlist.label: Pleomorphic adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass in the ear canal and histological features of pleomorphic cells

shortlist.label: Facial nerve hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Nonpulsatile mass in the inferior ear canal and imaging findings of expansion of the fallopian canal

shortlist.label: Geniculate ganglion hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Location of the mass near the stylomastoid foramen and geniculate ganglion

raw.rationale: The patient's 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness, nonpulsatile mass in the inferior ear canal, and imaging findings of an irregular lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen are consistent with a facial nerve schwannoma. The microscopic examination showing pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei and positive S100 staining also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Chondrosarcoma
rejected.why: While the gross examination showed a cartilage specimen, the microscopic findings and clinical presentation are more consistent with a facial nerve schwannoma

rejected.label: Pleomorphic adenoma
rejected.why: This diagnosis is less likely given the location of the tumor and the absence of typical salivary gland tumor features

rejected.label: Facial nerve hemangioma
rejected.why: The imaging findings and microscopic examination do not support a hemangioma diagnosis

rejected.label: Geniculate ganglion hemangioma
rejected.why: The location of the tumor and the clinical presentation are not consistent with a geniculate ganglion hemangioma
